q: Biology is the _____ of Life.
e: Biology is regarded as the Science of Life and the study of living things.

q: Morphology is the study of _____ and form.
e: Morphology is the study of structure and form of organisms.

q: Cytology is the study of _____ structure.
e: Cytology is the study of cell structure and function.

q: Biophysics studies flight of bird or _____ in bats.
e: Biophysics applies laws of physics to study biological processes like echolocation in bats.

q: Biochemistry studies _____ substances in cells.
e: Biochemistry is the study of chemical substances and processes in cells.

q: Biogeography explains distribution through _____.
e: Biogeography explains how plants and animals are distributed through space and time.

q: Biometry is Biology plus _____.
e: Biometry is the link between Biology and Statistic.

q: Anatomy and Histology are _____ science.
e: Anatomy and Histology study basic facts and are regarded as pure science.

q: Biotechnology and Veterinary science are _____ biology.
e: Biotechnology and Veterinary science are known as applied biology.

q: Agriculture breeds livestock for _____.
e: Agriculture and animal husbandry involve breeding of livestock for food.

q: Weather changes are caused by _____.
e: Weather changes are caused by the effect of global warming.

q: Over fishing and _____ lead to feeding problems.
e: Over fishing, over hunting and deforestation may lead to problems in feeding the population.

q: Biology is a fundamental _____ science.
e: Biology is a fundamental and important natural science.

q: Medicine restores and maintains _____ in humans.
e: Medicine is for restoration and maintenance of health in human.

q: Animal husbandry is farming of crops and breeding of _____.
e: Animal husbandry is farming of crops and breeding of livestock for food.

q: Identification assigns a _____ name.
e: Identification is the process in which an organism is assigned a scientific name.

q: Taxonomy is the study of _____.
e: The study and process of classification is known as Taxonomy.

q: Hierarchical classification has _____ taxa.
e: There are eight taxonomic groups or taxa in hierarchical classification.

q: Top three domains are Archaea, Bacteria, _____.
e: At the top of the hierarchical are three domains: Archaea, Bacteria and Eukarya.

q: Domains are subdivided into _____ levels.
e: Each domain is subdivided into seven different levels or taxa.

q: The lowest taxonomic level is _____.
e: The seven taxa levels end with Genus and Species.

q: Cladistics compares _____ to find relatedness.
e: In cladistics, techniques include comparing DNA from different species.

q: Dichotomous means divided into _____ parts.
e: The word dichotomous means divided into two parts.

q: Keys divide groups into two categories _____.
e: Dichotomous keys divide groups of organisms into two categories repeatedly.

q: Keys progress from general to more _____ characteristics.
e: Dichotomous keys progress to more specific characteristics step by step.

q: Thallophyta has no _____ formation.
e: In plant divisions, Thallophyta has no embryo formation.

q: Bryophyta has spores and _____ formation.
e: Bryophyta has spores and gametes formation.

q: Pteridophyta are _____-bearing with vascular system.
e: Pteridophyta are spore-bearing plants with vascular system.

q: Gymnospermae are non-flowering, _____-bearing.
e: Gymnospermae are non-flowering, seed-bearing plants.

q: Angiospermae are _____ plants.
e: Angiospermae are flowering plants.

q: Fish have fins and body covered with _____.
e: Fish are cold-blooded with body covered with scales and has fins.

q: Amphibians have body _____ covered with scales.
e: Amphibians are cold-blooded animals with body not covered with scales.

q: Reptiles have four limbs or _____ limbs.
e: Reptiles have four limbs or without limbs.

q: Birds are warm-blooded with _____.
e: Birds are warm-blooded animals with feathers present on body.

q: Mammals are warm-blooded with _____.
e: Mammals are warm-blooded animals with hair present on body.

q: Biologists use morphology and _____ as keys.
e: Biologists usually use easily identifiable features like morphology and anatomy.

q: Keys provide a simple way to _____ organisms.
e: Keys provide a simple way to classify organisms.

q: Cold-blooded vertebrates include Fish, Amphibian and _____.
e: Fish, Amphibian and Reptile are cold-blooded vertebrate classes.

q: Light microscope uses _____ as radiation source.
e: The light microscope uses light as a source of radiation.

q: Electron microscope uses _____ as radiation source.
e: The electron microscope uses electron as a source of radiation.

q: TEM allows us to see _____ sections.
e: In TEM, electron is passed through specimen to see thin sections.

q: SEM passes beam over the _____ of specimen.
e: In SEM, the electron beam is passed over the surface of the specimen.

q: Condenser focuses _____ onto the specimen.
e: Condenser focuses the light onto the specimen on the slide.

q: Objective lens is responsible for magnification and _____.
e: The objective lens is responsible for both magnification and resolution.

q: Eyepiece lens magnifies but does not _____ the image.
e: Eyepiece lens magnifies but does not resolve the image.

q: Iris diaphragm controls amount of _____.
e: By adjusting the iris diaphragm, the amount of light is controlled.

q: Electron microscope components must be in a _____.
e: The electron beam, specimen and screen must be in the vacuum.

q: Condenser electromagnetic lens focuses the _____ beam.
e: Condenser electromagnetic lens focuses the electron beam onto the specimen.

q: Projector lenses focus image onto the _____.
e: Projector electromagnetic lenses focus the magnified image onto the screen.

q: Light microscope magnifies up to _____.
e: The light microscope magnifies up to 2000X.

q: Electron microscope magnifies up to _____.
e: The electron microscope magnifies up to 500,000X.

q: Light microscope can examine _____ specimen.
e: Either dead or alive specimen can be examined in light microscope.

q: Electron microscope examines only _____ specimen.
e: Only dehydrated and dead specimen can be examined in electron microscope.

q: Specimen prep for electron microscope is _____.
e: Preparation of specimen for electron microscope is lengthy and complicated.

q: Magnification is number of times larger an image is compared to _____ size.
e: Magnification is the number of times larger an image is compared with the real size.

q: In $M = I / A$, $I$ is the _____ size.
e: $I$ stands for Observed (image) size of the specimen.

q: In $M = I / A$, $A$ is the _____ size.
e: $A$ stands for Actual size of the specimen.

q: Resolution is ability to distinguish between _____ objects close together.
e: Resolution is the ability to distinguish between two objects that are close together.

q: Increase in magnification might make image _____.
e: An increase in magnification does not always produce detail; the image may become blur.

q: Greater resolution means greater _____.
e: With resolution, the greater the resolution, the greater the detail.

q: Electron microscope image is recorded in _____.
e: The image of the specimen in electron microscope is in black and white.

q: Usually _____ illumination is the light source.
e: Usually substage illumination is the light source.

q: Electron gun emits _____ velocity electron beam.
e: Electron gun and anode emit high velocity electron beam.

q: Objective electromagnetic lens _____ the first image.
e: Objective electromagnetic lens focuses and magnified the first image.

q: Light passing through specimen is collected by _____ lens.
e: Light passing through the specimen is collected by the objective lens.

q: Biotechnology combines biological sciences with _____ technologies.
e: Biotechnology combines biological sciences with engineering technologies.

q: Traditional biotechnology includes making wine, cheese, yoghurt, bread and _____.
e: Traditional biotechnology includes making wine, cheese, yoghurt, bread and beer.

q: Mesopotamia used bacteria to convert wine into _____.
e: People in Mesopotamia used bacteria to convert wine into vinegar.

q: Modern biotechnology produces antibiotic _____.
e: Modern biotechnology produces medicines like antibiotic penicillin.

q: Human _____ producing genes are put into bacteria.
e: Human insulin producing genes are put into bacteria.

q: Transgenic goats produce antibodies in their _____.
e: Transgenic goats produce antibodies and blood clotting agent in their milk.

q: Transgenic plants are engineered to produce _____.
e: Transgenic plants are engineered to produce vaccine.

q: Microorganisms include protists, archea, fungi, bacteria and _____.
e: The term microorganisms include protists, archea, fungi, bacteria and viruses.

q: Archea and bacteria are _____.
e: Archea and bacteria are prokaryotes.

q: Viruses reproduce inside living cell using _____ materials of host.
e: Viruses reproduce using the genetic materials of the host.

q: Yeasts have single _____ cells.
e: Yeasts have single spherical cells.

q: Microorganisms are cultured easily by using _____.
e: Microorganisms can be cultured easily by using fermenters.

q: Biofuel fermentation produces _____ which is distilled.
e: This fermentation process produces ethanol which is distilled.

q: Ethanol is mixed with petrol to get _____.
e: It is mixed with petrol to get gasohol.

q: In bread making, water activates _____ enzymes.
e: Water activates the amylase enzymes to act on the starch.

q: Yeasts ferment sugar to carbon dioxide and _____.
e: Yeasts ferment the sugar to carbon dioxide and ethanol.

q: Protein _____ holds carbon dioxide gas bubbles in dough.
e: A sticky protein gluten holds the carbon dioxide gas bubbles.

q: Dough is baked in oven at _____ to kill yeasts.
e: The dough is baked in the oven at $200^{\circ}	ext{C}$.

q: Milk is pasteurized at about _____ to kill bacteria.
e: Milk is pasteurized at about $90^{\circ}	ext{C}$ degree.

q: Starter culture turns lactose to _____.
e: The bacteria turn the lactose to lactic acid.

q: Lactic acid coagulates milk protein _____.
e: This acid coagulates the milk protein casein.

q: In cheese making, _____ causes further coagulation.
e: A mixture of enzymes called rennet causes further coagulation.

q: Grape juice is treated with sulphur dioxide to kill _____ yeast.
e: Treated with sulphur dioxide to kill the natural occurring yeast.

q: Yeast respire aerobically until _____ is used up.
e: Respire aerobically at first until the oxygen is used up.

q: Yeast cells die when alcohol content reaches _____.
e: When the alcohol content reach 15%, the yeast cells die.

q: Beer is made from barley grains which activate _____-digesting enzymes.
e: Germinate thus activating the starch-digesting enzymes.

q: The sugary solution obtained from malted barley is called _____.
e: A sugary solution called wort is obtained.

q: Wort is boiled with hops which give beer a _____ flavour.
e: Boiled with hops which give beer a bitter flavour.

q: Louis Pasteur described alcoholic fermentation as 'life without _____'.
e: Louis Pasteur described alcoholic fermentation as life without air.

q: Fermenter tanks are made of stainless steel to withstand _____ effect.
e: Made of stainless steel to withstand the corroding effect.

q: Hot _____ is passed into fermenter to sterilize it.
e: Hot steam is passed into the fermenter to sterilize it.

q: Enzymes are protein molecules and biological _____.
e: Enzymes are protein molecules and biological catalysts.

q: Enzymes do not require expensive fuel to maintain high _____.
e: Do not require expensive fuel to maintain high temperature.

q: Microbial trypsin is used to treat blood _____.
e: Microbial trypsin is used to treat blood clotting.

q: Pancreatic trypsin is used for treatment of _____.
e: Pancreatic trypsin is used for treatment of inflammation.

q: Proteases are _____-digesting enzymes.
e: Proteases are the protein-digesting enzymes.

q: Lipases are _____-digesting enzymes.
e: Lipases are the fat-digesting enzymes.

q: Proteases act on red _____ in blood stains.
e: The enzyme proteases act on red haemoglobin.

q: Fungi produce _____ enzymes for extracting fruit juices.
e: Fungi produce the pectinases enzymes.

q: Pectinases break down pectin between cell walls and separate fruit _____.
e: Break down pectin and separate the fruit cells.

q: Break down of polysaccharides causes juice to become _____.
e: Polysaccharides released causing the juice to become cloudy.

q: Pectinases break polysaccharides to sugar making juice sweeter and _____.
e: Making the juice sweeter and clearer.

q: Biological washing powders remove stains caused by blood, egg, gravy and _____.
e: Stains caused by blood, egg, gravy and grease.

q: Enzymes isolated from cell still retain their ability to _____.
e: Enzymes isolated from the cell still retain their ability to function.

q: Many industrial enzymes are obtained from fungi or _____.
e: Many enzymes are obtained from microorganisms mostly from fungi or bacteria.

q: Both protein and fat molecules are large but enzymes digest them into small, _____ substances.
e: Digest them into small, soluble substances which pass out of the fabric.
